summary: Lal Mani Joshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur under Govind Chandra Pande, later holding posts at Gorakhpur, Punjabi University, Haverford, Amherst, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi worked in Indology, serving as a Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Baroda and holding an attested post at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, in 1939.

Lama Jampa Thaye is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a PhD from the University of Manchester, studied with traditional teachers including Karma Thinley Rinpoche, and joined the international teaching faculty at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

Lama Kunga Rinpoche is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ngor Monastery, where he served as Thartse Shabthung in 1959. In 1973, he founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center.

Lama Palden Drolma is a specialist in Buddhist and religious studies who was trained by traditional teachers including the 16th Karmapa, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Tai Situ Rinpoche, and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

Lama Thubten Yeshe was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar trained at Sera Monastery under teachers including Geshe Rabten. He founded the FPMT, Kopan Monastery, and Tushita Meditation Centre, and taught at the universities of Virginia and California, Santa Cruz.

Lama Tsultrim Allione is a scholar and practitioner in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a master's degree at Antioch University, studied under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa and the 16th Karmapa, and founded Tara Mandala in 1993.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso works in the fields of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche and Lama Norlha.

Lambert Schmithausen is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar who earned his doctorate under Erich Frauwallner. He was an associate professor at the University of Münster (1970–1973) and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University in 1986 and later served as a professor at the University of San Diego.

Lance S. Cousins worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and Kenneth Roy Norman. He taught at Manchester and Oxford, served as President of the Pali Text Society, and was a fellow at Wolfson College.
Lang Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed a PhD at Yale University, where she was supervised by Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff.
Lang Eun Ra is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral studies at Temple University under the supervision of Charles Wei-hsun Fu.
Lara Braitstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University, where she studied under Richard P. Hayes.
Laren Hogen Bays is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner who studied under Shodo Harada. In 2002, he founded the Great Vow Zen Monastery, where he serves as co-abbot.

Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Minnesota. He held teaching or research posts at Minnesota, Hawaiʻi, Washington, Chicago, and Langara College.

Lars Fogelin specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli and held positions at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.
Lars Martin Fosse is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Oslo, Heidelberg University, and the University of Bonn, and taught at the University of Oslo.

Lati Rinpoche was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Geshe Lharampa degree at Ganden Shartse Monastery and studied at Gyuto. He served as abbot of Ganden and Ganden Shartse monasteries and was a visiting scholar at Virginia.

Latika Lahiri was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji from 1956 to 1958. She held an academic post at the University of Delhi from around 1969 to 1988.
